analysis.title: The Flow Show: Sell Signal Ends
key_insights: The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator fell from 8.1 to 7.4. A reading below 8.0 ends the sell signal triggered May 26. The drop was driven by weaker global stock index breadth, bearish hedge fund positions in oil and S&P 500 futures, less bullish gold futures positioning and weaker HY and EM debt flows, partly offset by stronger tech inflows. The indicator's current signal is Neutral.
Since the May 26 sell signal, SPX is +3.0% (max drawdown -4.5%), NDX -0.2% (max drawdown -11.3%), ACWI +1.1% (max drawdown -4.4%) and JNK junk bonds -4.1% (max drawdown -4.7%).

BofA says the summer of extreme bull sentiment has ended but asset allocators are not underweight risk. 2026 is on pace for record annualized inflows to global stocks ($1.3tn), US equities ($636bn), IG bonds ($480bn), tech funds ($196bn) and Korea equities ($76bn), against a record outflow from consumer funds ($18bn).

Weekly flows: $64.5bn into stocks, $11.8bn into bonds, $0.1bn into gold, $0.6bn out of crypto and $53.1bn out of cash. US stocks took $39.1bn, tech $10.7bn and EM stocks $17.7bn (the biggest since Jul'26, with $8.6bn into China and a record $4.7bn into Brazil over two weeks). Treasuries logged a 16th straight weekly inflow.

BofA private clients hold a record 66.4% in stocks, 9.3% in cash (a record low) and 17.1% in bonds (almost a record low). They are still adding stocks but have started to add Treasuries, up $11bn in 2-10 year USTs since Q1 and $4.5bn in T-bills since June. In ETFs over four weeks they bought municipal bond, bank loan and industrials ETFs and sold staples, EM debt and consumer discretionary ETFs.

The BofA Breadth Rule shows net 52% of global equity indices oversold (below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages), the most since Apr'25. A buy signal needs net 88%. BofA says that is unlikely near term unless the overbought US, Taiwan and Brazil indices fall 6%-10%.
Price action: BofA expects falling bond yields in October to improve equity breadth in Q4. 355 S&P 500 stocks trade 10% below their 52-week highs, 188 trade 20% below and 93 trade 30% below.

Near-term stance: BofA leans risk-off for the next 3-4 weeks. The reasons given are 3% US 10-year real yields, the need for the Fed to hike on Oct 28, US/Iran/Russia/Ukraine/oil risk, the risk of a wave-like Democratic sweep in the midterms, and weakness in AI spenders and lenders (BIZD, PSP, Oracle CDS).

BofA expects a Fed October hike to restore credibility, as CPI has been above the 2% target for 66 consecutive months. It says the hike should cut long-end Treasury yields another 20bps in coming weeks. That would limit downside for risk assets if AI financing fears abate and there are no big US-China spats after the midterms. Xi and Trump are noted to meet at Shenzhen APEC on Nov 18 and Miami G20 on Dec 14.

Positioning advice: add 'peak yield' beneficiaries, namely small cap, REITs and especially consumer discretionary. The October FMS shows investors the most underweight consumer discretionary since Jul'08. Do not add tech, since the FMS shows investors the most overweight tech since Aug'20 and an AI bubble in '27 is now consensus. Long term, stay long gold, commodities and emerging markets. BofA says secular short or underweight positions in bonds and China need to be reduced.

AI thesis for '27: BofA expects macro and markets into '27 to be driven by AI and says to watch semiconductor prices (US PPI semiconductors). Fresh price gains are bullish. A rollover in semi prices would signal tighter AI credit, a top in AI capex growth and lower-than-expected nominal GDP growth in '27, with asset returns then driven by income rather than capital appreciation. BofA expects investors to return to tech in mid-Nov.

AI financing strain: chart labels show consensus hyperscaler capex rising from $412bn ('25) to $807bn ('26) and $1163bn ('27), with free cash flow turning from $191bn ('25) to -$63bn ('26) and -$163bn ('27). The chart is headed 'Hyperscaler FCF flips negative on AI spending arms race'. BDC and private equity ETFs are back at 1H26 or '25 lows, and Oracle 5-year CDS is plotted against US IG tech spreads as a sign of tightening AI credit.
Korea: South Korea equity funds are annualizing a record $76bn inflow YTD. For every $100 of Korea inflow YTD, just $7 has left since the August peak, while KOSPI is -30% from its June peak.

Currencies: the Indian rupee, Indonesian rupiah and Turkish lira are at or near all-time lows against the dollar, and the yen is 3% from 40-year lows. Five-year depreciation is TRY -81%, JPY -28%, INR -21% and IDR -21%.

YTD cross-asset returns: oil +70.0%, US stocks +13.1%, global stocks +10.2%, USD +3.8%, cash +2.9%, HY bonds -0.9%, IG -3.2%, government bonds -4.4%, gold -4.5% and bitcoin -6.1%. In the dollar-terms ranking table, Korea equities lead country returns at +72.9% and Taiwan is +70.4%. India equities are the weakest at -14.3% and China -12.7%.

Sector flows this week: inflows to tech ($10.7bn), energy ($1.3bn), healthcare ($1.2bn) and real estate ($0.3bn). Outflows from financials ($1.4bn), consumer ($0.6bn), utilities, communication services and materials. By region, Japan saw inflows resume ($0.4bn) and Europe saw outflows resume ($1.5bn).

tension_points.bull_case: Semiconductor prices rising would be bullish. The AI spending arms race between the US and China continues, and BofA says the US government guarantees bond and equity prices will not be allowed to impede the US. Investors then return to tech in mid-Nov and enter '27 reversing 'short tech bond' positions.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus hyperscaler free cash flow turns negative in '26 and '27 on rising capex. BDC and private equity ETFs are back at 1H26 or '25 lows, Oracle 5-year CDS is elevated, and investors are the most overweight tech since Aug'20.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rollover in semiconductor prices (US PPI semiconductors), which BofA says signals tighter AI credit, a top in AI capex growth and lower-than-expected nominal GDP growth in '27.

tension_points.theme: Fed October hike and risk assets
tension_points.bull_case: A hike restores Fed credibility after 66 months of CPI above 2%, cuts long-end yields another 20bps and limits downside for risk assets.
tension_points.bear_case: 3% real yields, the Fed hike itself, geopolitics and midterm risk support a risk-off lean for the next 3-4 weeks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI financing fears worsening or a new US-China spat after the midterms would undercut the limited-downside view.
